We are reaching for the stars and together we might just get there. Open communication, asking hard questions and valuing diverse viewpoints are but a few things that will help us achieve our goals. Above all we will never stop learning and striving to help each other reach our maximum potential.

Please note that for this Software Engineer GTM Products role, we are only considering candidates based in Eastern Europe, the Baltics, or the Balkans.

Responsibilities

  • Productionize prototypes. Take AI-built prototypes from the GTM team and make them real: authentication and access scoping, error handling, data integrity, tests, monitoring, documentation, handover.

  • Own the infrastructure. Hosting, environments, CI/CD, secrets, backups, dependencies and releases for every GTM-owned service.

  • Own security for partner-facing software. Authentication and role/hierarchy scoping, handling of partner and end-customer data, and answering the security questions partners and enterprise customers ask.

  • Own the code. Repositories, code review, feature flags, and the standard a prototype has to meet before it ships - including the authority to send one back.

  • Run rollouts. Staged releases, pilot partners, rollback plans, in cooperation with the GTM team communication that goes with a release.

  • Build an integrated solution landscape. The future is about data - this role works with our internal data, process and product specialists to build the integration system that allows to use the right data in the right way across all tools and departments

  • Context infrastructure. You co-own the context layer that is used for our GTM, sales, csm and other agents. 

  • Contribute to the AI engineering practice for Wingtra. Co-create the future of coding in a fast growing scaleup!


    • Requirements

  • A university degree in software engineering or computer science

  • Engineer who has operated software, not only built it. 3+ years full-stack; has run a customer-facing web application in production and been on the hook when it broke. TypeScript / Next.js, Postgres, a modern hosting platform.

  • AI-native. Coding agents are their default way of working, and they can review, harden and take ownership of code they did not write.

  • Security-literate practitioner. Authn/authz, multi-tenant scoping, secrets management, data-protection basics - enough to be the accountable owner without a security team behind them.

  • Integration-heavy background. CRM and ERP APIs (HubSpot, Odoo or equivalent), webhooks, and reconciling data across systems that disagree.

  • Product Management Experience. You can handle internal & external customer interactions and working with product management best practices

  • Holds a standard at a distance. Writes decisions down, communicates without being asked, and can send work back to people they rarely sit next to — including to this role’s own manager.


    • Plus

  • Commercial fluency. Reads a pricing model, a channel margin and a renewal term and understands why the business cares. Useful, not required - GTM brings the commercial framing, this role brings the engineering.

  • Experience in a partner or channel business, or with any two-tier distribution model

  • Has productionized other people’s prototypes before — an internal tools or platform team background

    • If you enjoy teamwork more than being the individual superhero, and if you thrive in a feedback-driven culture and an exciting, unconventional yet structured and progressive start-up environment, we would love to hear from you.

description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied ML Engineer based in Switzerland. As an Applied ML Engineer, you’ll work at the intersection of machine learning research, experimentation, and production engineering. You’ll turn ideas from research papers into rigorous experiments, measurable evidence, and reliable products. The role spans model evaluation, model internals, inference infrastructure, backend systems, and user-facing product experiences. You’ll work hands-on with modern ML models, designing evaluations that reveal what methods can—and cannot—demonstrate. You’ll also build production-grade tooling that makes complex experiments repeatable, observable, and accessible to users. The environment values technical judgment, ownership, scientific rigor, and the ability to move comfortably across the technology stack. It’s an opportunity to help transform emerging ML techniques into practical systems that people can trust. Accountabilities Reproduce and evaluate machine learning research methods using open-weight and API-accessible models. raw.description:
About RIVR, part of Amazon 

RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI through real-world doorstep delivery. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn from rich operational data at scale. 

Following our acquisition by Amazon in March 2026, we are continuing this mission with greater reach and speed. By combining custom robot hardware, onboard autonomy, and cloud-based coordination, RIVR, part of Amazon is building the next generation of safe, reliable autonomous robots for last-mile delivery. 


Job Description

We are looking for a Technical Lead – Testing Engineer to own and elevate the testing strategy for our advanced robotic systems. In this role you will define how we validate hardware reliability and performance, from individual actuator characterization through full system-level integration. You will lead a team of test engineers, set technical directions and goals for test infrastructure, and be the bridge between technical unknowns and experimental measurements that enable engineering decisions ultimately shaping our robots. 

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will still design test benches, write automation code, and dig into data, but you will also mentor engineers, drive process maturity, and represent testing in cross-functional planning. If you combine deep technical expertise in hardware testing with the ability to set priorities, grow people, and influence design outcomes, this role offers a unique opportunity to shape how a Physical AI company validates its products. 


What you'll be doing 
 

Technical Leadership & Strategy 

  • Define and own the end-to-end test strategy for structural, mechatronic, and sensing subsystems, aligned with product development milestones. 

  • Establish testing standards, processes, and best practices across the team, including test plan templates, data management workflows, and reporting formats. 

  • Make architectural decisions on test infrastructure: investments into instrumentation platforms, automation frameworks, and data pipelines. 

  • Drive continuous improvement of test coverage, efficiency, and predictive capability. 

Hands-On Testing & Engineering 

  • Design, commission, and operate test benches for mechatronics systems (actuators, mechanism, cabling and sensor), including fixture design, instrumentation layout, and safety concepts. 

  • Select, integrate, and calibrate sensors, load cells, thermocouples with a thorough understanding of their working principles and error influences. 

  • Develop and maintain automation scripts (Python, Labview) to control test hardware, execute stress and performance tests, and log critical data. 

  • Process and analyze test data applying signal processing and statistics fundamental to extract meaningful performance metrics. 

Reporting & Design Influence 

  • Compile clear, structured test reports that compare results against specifications, highlight anomalies, and derive actionable engineering learnings to feed back into the design cycle. 

  • Identify failure modes, performance bottlenecks, and reliability risks, translating findings into concrete design recommendations. 

  • Represent the test function in design reviews, providing data-driven input on FMEA, and qualification criteria. 

Team & Collaboration 

  • Mentor and grow test engineers, fostering technical depth and a culture of rigorous, curiosity-driven experimentation. 

  • Collaborate closely with mechanical, electrical, firmware, and systems engineers to align test strategies with product requirements. 

  • Coordinate with external test labs and suppliers when specialized testing is required. 


Basic Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related technical field. 

  • 7+ years of experience in hardware testing or validation, with at least 3 years in a technical leadership or senior individual contributor role. 

  • Proven experience designing and commissioning test benches for electro-mechanical system or consumer electronics with significant power and motion elements. 

  • Strong scripting proficiency in Python for test automation, device control, and data analysis. 

  • Practical knowledge of sensors and instrumentation — torque cells, encoders, load cells, thermocouples, strain gauges, including their working principles, error influences, and calibration requirements. 

  • Demonstrated ability to turn test data into clear engineering insights that influence design decisions. 

  • Experience developing and reviewing test plans, test cases, and qualification criteria. 

  • The ability to work hands-on in a workshop environment and use common tools safely. 


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with motor or actuator characterization (efficiency mapping, cogging-torque analysis, thermal correlation). 

  • Familiarity with test automation frameworks (LabVIEW, pytest) or hardware-in-the-loop setups. 

  • Understanding of measurement uncertainty analysis (GUM) and calibration procedures. 

  • Hands-on experience with ROS/ROS2. 

  • Experience with CAD software (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) for designing test fixtures. 

  • Knowledge of data acquisition (DAQ) hardware and system integration. 

  • Experience working in robotics, automotive, or aerospace test environments. 

  • Track record of building or scaling a test engineering function within a fast-moving hardware team. 

RIVR, part of Amazon is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that values every perspective. If you're passionate about driving innovation in robotics and creating meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply and bring your unique self to our team. 

We believe the best work is done when collaborating and therefore require in-person presence in our office locations.

In environments without existing maps, the robot must dynamically create a map while simultaneously localizing itself within it. As our next SLAM Engineer on a growing team, you will be an expert in laser- and camera-based localization techniques and SLAM and enhance these capabilities. You will shape our robots’ ability to navigate with pinpoint precision, and you will be part of a team focused on enabling our robots to navigate autonomously. If you are passionate about robotics and driven to innovate in SLAM and localization, we encourage you to join us in shaping the future of intelligent robotics. Responsibilities Develop state-of-the-art, online and offline localization and SLAM algorithms by fusing information from cameras, LiDARs, IMU, GNSS, and other sensors. Design, validate, and improve algorithms on challenging real-world data. Contribute to the dynamic mapping of the environment using data continuously gathered from ongoing robot deployments. Assist in the creation of robust sensor calibration systems that perform reliably in complex and unpredictable environments. Support the development of an efficient workflow to accurately capture ground truth data, and maps of deployment sites for algorithm evaluation. Contribute to the implementation of deployment-ready code for the real robot, optimized for the robot’s computational constraints. title: Senior Electronics Engineer – Functional Safety
description: RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI through real-world doorstep delivery. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn from rich operational data at scale. Following our acquisition by Amazon in March 2026, we are continuing this mission with greater reach and speed. By combining custom robot hardware, onboard autonomy, and cloud-based coordination, RIVR, part of Amazon is building the next generation of safe, reliable autonomous robots for last-mile delivery. Job Description As a Senior Electronics Engineer – Functional Safety, you will own the hardware-level Functional Safety design for our robots’ custom electronics. You will design fault-tolerant circuits at the schematic and PCB level — implementing redundant architectures, hardware diagnostics, and safe-state mechanisms — and perform the quantitative reliability analysis to substantiate that your designs meet the required Safety Integrity Level. This is a hands-on circuit design role, not a systems-level safety concept or process management position. What You’ll Be Doing Design fault-tolerant circuits for safety-critical subsystems, selecting appropriate safety architectures (e.g., 1oo2, 1oo2D) based on the required SIL target. Implement hardware diagnostic and monitoring mechanisms to detect dangerous failures. Design circuits that enforce a defined safe state when a fault is detected. Apply Common-Cause Failure mitigation techniques at the component and PCB level. Perform FMEDA on your own schematics — identifying failure modes per component and calculating Safe Failure Fraction (SFF) and Diagnostic Coverage (DC). Build Reliability Block Diagrams and compute SIL metrics to verify your designs meet the target. Select and derate components based on failure rate data, mission profiles, and expected lifetime. Advise system architects on hardware safety constraints and review PCB layouts for safety compliance. Collaborate with electronics, firmware, and systems engineering teams to integrate safety functions into the overall robot design. Create and maintain Functional Safety documentation for your hardware modules. What You Must Have Master’s degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a closely related field. 5+ years  designing electronics hardware for Functional Safety–certified products. Proven work under  IEC 61508  (preferred), ISO 13849, or ISO 26262. Delivered PCB-level hardware that achieved  SIL 2 or SIL 3  (or equivalent PL d/e, ASIL B–D) certification. Background in  analog, power, and/or mixed-signal circuit design . Hands-on experience implementing safety architectures in schematics — not just block diagrams. Ability to perform FMEDA and SIL metrics calculations on your own designs. Understanding of failure rate data sources and component derating for reliability. Strong problem-solving skills and ability to debug fault-tolerant hardware. Comfortable working cross-functionally with firmware, mechanical, and systems teams. Get Some Bonus Points Experience with safety-rated ICs (safe supply supervisors, safety MCUs, smart drivers with diagnostic feedback). Has contributed to or authored a Safety Manual for a hardware module. Familiar with Proven-in-Use argumentation for off-the-shelf components. PCB layout skills relevant to safety (creepage/clearance, redundant channel routing). Experience with circuit simulation (SPICE) to verify fault response behaviour. Experience in robotics, automotive, aerospace, or medical device sectors. PhD degree in a relevant engineering discipline. raw.title: Procurement Engineer
raw.description:
About RIVR, part of Amazon  

RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI through real-world doorstep delivery. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn from rich operational data at scale. 

Following our acquisition by Amazon in March 2026, we are continuing this mission with greater reach and speed. By combining custom robot hardware, onboard autonomy, and cloud-based coordination, RIVR, part of Amazon is building the next generation of safe, reliable autonomous robots for last-mile delivery. 


Job Description
As the Procurement Engineer at RIVR, you will be the dedicated technical-business bridge in our Zürich office, designed to take the "negotiation load" off our core engineering team. 

We need a professional who can independently manage the procurement of complex robot components - from PCBs to custom mechanical assemblies - handling six-figure capital expenditures for mission-critical robotics infrastructure. 

In this role, you will operate as a significant and autonomous contributor. You will solve difficult procurement challenges by applying technical best practices and materials knowledge. You will take ownership of vendor timelines and price negotiations that were previously handled by engineers, ensuring our designers can stay focused on innovation while you ensure our hardware arrives on time, on quality, and on budget. 


What You’ll Be Doing
This is a multifaceted role requiring a blend of technical literacy and a proactive spirit to manage a fast-paced startup environment during our scaling phase. You will work with limited guidance to professionalize our supply chain workflows.
 

● Act as the primary point of contact for technical suppliers, managing all communications regarding pricing, quality issues,  lead times, and contract terms. 

● Independently manage the purchasing for robot-specific commodities: PCBs, custom cables, metallic and non-metallic components.

● Lead the evolution of our material tracking from manual spreadsheets into professionalized workflows, preparing the organization for future ERP implementation. 

● Partner with the CTO in Zürich and the Head of Supply Chain in Shanghai to ensure engineering requirements are perfectly translated into production plans. 

● Proactively identify supply chain risks, such as raw material shortages or price surges, and develop decisive mitigation strategies. 

● Assist engineers in making the right "make vs. buy" decisions and provide detailed cost-justification studies for high-value orders. 

● Support the transition of hardware from the concept/prototype phase into volume production by managing initial vendor technical reviews. 

● Ensure all procured parts meet RIVR’s high standards for durability, performance, and safety requirements. 

● Communicate findings and constructively propose ideas or corrections to hardware specifications to non-technical partners. 

● Optimize best practices for validation and test processes related to incoming hardware. 

● Track supplier part delivery status to ensure quality and timeliness. 

● Maintain supplier relationships and continuously feed industrial insights back into the engineering backlog. 

● Cooperate with suppliers from Europe, China and the USA. 


What You Must Have 

● Proven experience in technical procurement, buying, or supply chain management in a hardware-centric industry. 

● Proven track record of managing and negotiating substantial purchase orders and vendor contracts. 

● Ability to understand technical drawings and engineering specifications for mechanical and electrical components. 

● Ability to take lead in an environment where processes are still evolving; a strong "bias for action" and clarity. 

● Ability to make the right hardware design trade-offs (e.g., make vs. buy, OEM vs. ODM). 

● Exceptional verbal and written English; ability to harmonize views between international teams. 


Bonus Points

● Skills in bottom-up cost analysis and should-cost modeling for custom-machined or injection-molded parts. 

● Experience in an early-stage startup or a high-pressure "overdrive" environment. 

● Ability to use prototyping or schematic capture software (e.g., CAD, MATLAB). 

● Experience with ERP systems or supporting a first-time ERP implementation. 

● Experience with suppliers from all over the world.
